content:
I am doing something a bit similar to verso, but with typst. I have many modules with literate Lean, for example Foo.lean:

import Typst

#typst[
  = Hello
  Test
]

Currently, the #typst[...] command simply appends the generated Typst as a String to an environment extension. I quite like this approach, because it lets me see the typst file update live as I type, using a very low-tech solution with a custom #saveTypst "./Foo.lean.typ" command at the end of every file. I want to make this nicer, so that I don't have to write #saveTypst in every file.

I know Lake facets exist, and they might be what I want, but I am not sure. I want every module Foo.lean to produce a corresponding Foo.lean.typ file. Can I do this with Lake facets? I already have the generated Typst I want to save as a String, I just need to save it to a corresponding file.

I had a look at verso's lakefile, and it seems to build verso-literate and run it as a system command. I don't think this is what I want; I want the corresponding typst file to update live as I type, not only when I run lake build.
You could make your env extension code update the file during elaboration.
With lake facets you still have to build e.g. lake build Foo:facet_name

Just to be clear about the situation, you may have multiple #typst commands in a file, and the resulting Strings all get incorporated into the same output file, right? So you need to run it at the end?

There is a not-so-secret technique for this sort of thing... :) You can lint the eoi (end of input) token at the end of every lean file, and in the linter read the environment extension & write to the file. (You could hypothetically also elaborate the eoi token, but I don't think you need to adjust the environment itself, right? That's all you would need elaboration for...and ideally this would be extensible via some @[cleanup] attribute. Aside: I made the extensible version for skimmer, then took a different approach. Maybe it belongs somewhere else, though...batteries?) Search mathlib for "eoi" to see some examples :)

This is indeed a bit of a hack, though. A lake facet would give you some extra control, perhaps? But probably wouldn't give you a live view, and you'd have to call it specially as Adam said.
